History:
• Chief concern: Progressive numbness, tingling, and subjective weakness of the left upper limb.  
• Onset & course: Began ≈2 weeks ago after starting a boxing class; initial mild tingling has progressed to constant numbness from elbow to hand.  
• Distribution: Palmar surface of 2nd-4th digits, forearm, occasional shoulder discomfort.  
• Functional impact: Difficulty playing piano; occasional object-handling weakness (no pain-limited grip).  
• Associated symptoms: One transient episode of partial visual loss in left eye (≈20 min, a few weeks ago); generalized fatigue; intermittent “tired” headaches. No neck pain, seizures, lower-limb weakness, gait change, or loss of consciousness.  
• Self-care tried: Massage, warm baths, ibuprofen – no improvement.  
• No recent trauma other than boxing activity; had a “bad cold/flu” ~1 month ago.

Past Medical History:
• Generally healthy; no chronic diagnoses documented.  
• Recent viral illness (self-reported).  
• Allergies: Not documented.  
• Medications/Supplements:  
  – Ibuprofen – dose/route/frequency not documented  
  – Vitamin D – dose/frequency not documented  
  – Iron supplement (inconsistent use) – dose not documented  
  – Melatonin – dose/frequency not documented  
• Family history: Father – hypothyroidism/autoimmune disease; Mother – type 2 diabetes, hypertension, hyperlipidemia; no known familial neurological disorders.

Physical Examination:
(teleconsultation – limited)  
• General: Patient alert, oriented, conversant.  
• Neurological (subjective): Sensory deficit (numbness) L 2nd-4th digits and forearm; subjective weakness left hand/arm. No reported lower-limb weakness, balance issues, or sphincter disturbance.  
• Eyes: Normal vision currently; no diplopia.  
• No other physical findings documented.

Impression:
Left upper-limb sensory deficit with episodic visual disturbance – rule out demyelinating disease (e.g., multiple sclerosis) versus compressive/traumatic neuropathy.

Management Plan:
• Arrange urgent neurology referral for further evaluation.  
• Anticipated investigations: MRI brain/spine, formal neurological examination.  
• No pharmacologic treatment initiated pending specialist assessment.  
• Safety-net advice: Attend emergency department if new or worsening neurological symptoms (leg weakness, persistent or worsening visual loss, severe headache, vomiting, seizures).  
• Continue current over-the-counter analgesia only if needed.

Patient Summary:
Ms. Mary Smith reports 2 weeks of progressive numbness and weakness in her left arm and a prior brief episode of left-eye visual loss. Findings raise concern for a central neurological process such as multiple sclerosis. She will receive an urgent neurology referral and MRI; instructed on red-flag symptoms requiring immediate care.

Key Takeaways:
• Seek emergency help if symptoms spread to legs, vision worsens, or severe headache/vomiting develops.  
• Await urgent neurology appointment and imaging; no new medications until assessed.  
• Limit boxing/upper-limb strain until cause clarified.

Next Steps:
• Neurology consult (urgent) with MRI brain ± cervical spine.  
• Formal neurological examination and optic assessment.  
• Review results with primary physician once available; adjust management accordingly.
